Northline Payments · API v1

Developer Integration Guide

Integrate card and bank payments, refunds, and payment-status webhooks against the Northline Payments REST API. This guide covers authentication, the resource model, request and response shapes, errors, and operational limits.

Contents
  1. Authentication
  2. Base URL

  6. Error codes
  7. Webhooks

Authentication

Every request is authenticated with a secret API key sent as a bearer token. Keys are scoped to an environment (test or live) and to a merchant account. Treat secret keys like passwords: store them in a secrets manager, never ship them in a mobile or browser app, and rotate them if they leak.

Send the key on every call:

Authorization: Bearer sk_test_YOUR_SECRET_KEY
Idempotency-Key: 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7
  • sk_test_… — test mode. Charges are simulated; no money moves.
  • sk_live_… — live mode. Charges settle to the linked bank account.
  • pk_test_… / pk_live_… — publishable keys, safe for client-side tokenization only. They cannot create charges.

Mutating requests (POST, and refunds) should include an Idempotency-Key header: a UUID you generate. Replaying the same key with the same body within 24 hours returns the original response instead of creating a second payment. A different body with a reused key returns 409 idempotency_key_reused.

Never log full card numbers, CVVs, or secret keys. Tokenize card data with the client SDK or a PCI-compliant vault, then charge the token server-side.

Base URL

All paths in this guide are relative to the versioned base URL. The version is pinned in the path so a later major version does not change existing integrations.

EnvironmentBase URL
Testhttps://api.sandbox.northlinepay.example/v1
Livehttps://api.northlinepay.example/v1

Use HTTPS only. Requests must send Content-Type: application/json and Accept: application/json. Amounts are integers in the currency’s minor unit (cents for USD, pence for GBP). Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC. Object IDs are prefixed strings such as pay_, cus_, and ref_.

Endpoints

Resources are JSON objects. List endpoints accept limit (1–100, default 20) and starting_after (an object ID) for cursor pagination. Successful creates return 201; reads return 200.

MethodPathPurpose
POST /payments Create a payment (authorize and capture, or authorize only).
GET /payments/{id} Retrieve a payment by ID.
GET /payments List payments. Filter with customer, status, created_gte.
POST /payments/{id}/capture Capture a previously authorized payment, in full or in part.
POST /refunds Refund a captured payment, in full or in part.
POST /customers Create a customer to store payment methods against.
GET /customers/{id} Retrieve a customer.
POST /payment_methods Attach a tokenized card or bank account to a customer.
POST /webhook_endpoints Register an HTTPS URL to receive event notifications.

Create payment — body fields

FieldRequiredNotes
amountYesInteger, minor units. Minimum 50 for USD.
currencyYesISO 4217, lowercase. Example: usd.
payment_methodYesID of a tokenized method, e.g. pm_card_visa.
customerNoCustomer ID. Required when reusing a saved method.
captureNoDefault true. Set false to authorize only.
descriptionNoShown on the customer’s statement descriptor suffix area and in your dashboard. Max 255 characters.
metadataNoUp to 20 key/value string pairs. Returned on the object and on webhooks.

Request and response examples

Create and capture a payment

Request body:

{
  "amount": 2499,
  "currency": "usd",
  "payment_method": "pm_card_visa",
  "customer": "cus_8f3a91c2",
  "capture": true,
  "description": "Order 10482 — wool coat",
  "metadata": {
    "order_id": "10482"
  }
}

Response 201 Created:

{
  "id": "pay_3k91ab20",
  "object": "payment",
  "amount": 2499,
  "amount_captured": 2499,
  "currency": "usd",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "customer": "cus_8f3a91c2",
  "payment_method": "pm_card_visa",
  "description": "Order 10482 — wool coat",
  "metadata": { "order_id": "10482" },
  "created": "2026-11-01T14:22:08Z"
}

status is one of requires_action, authorized, processing, succeeded, failed, or canceled. When the issuer requires 3-D Secure, status is requires_action and next_action.redirect_url is set. Send the customer to that URL; the result arrives as a webhook, not as a browser return you should trust alone.

Refund

Request body to POST /v1/refunds:

{
  "payment": "pay_3k91ab20",
  "amount": 500,
  "reason": "requested_by_customer"
}

Omit amount to refund the full captured amount. Response 201:

{
  "id": "ref_11c04e",
  "object": "refund",
  "payment": "pay_3k91ab20",
  "amount": 500,
  "currency": "usd",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "reason": "requested_by_customer",
  "created": "2026-11-02T09:01:44Z"
}

Error body

Failures use a single envelope. HTTP status matches the class of error; the machine-readable code is in error.code.

{
  "error": {
    "type": "card_error",
    "code": "card_declined",
    "message": "The card was declined.",
    "decline_code": "insufficient_funds",
    "payment": "pay_9aa01c",
    "request_id": "req_6f20c1d8"
  }
}

curl examples

Replace the key and IDs with values from your dashboard. These calls target the sandbox.

Create a payment

curl https://api.sandbox.northlinepay.example/v1/payments \
  -u sk_test_YOUR_SECRET_KEY: \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 2499,
    "currency": "usd",
    "payment_method": "pm_card_visa",
    "description": "Order 10482 — wool coat",
    "metadata": { "order_id": "10482" }
  }'

-u key: sends HTTP Basic auth with an empty password, which the API accepts as equivalent to Authorization: Bearer.

Retrieve a payment

curl https://api.sandbox.northlinepay.example/v1/payments/pay_3k91ab20 \
  -u sk_test_YOUR_SECRET_KEY:

Partial refund

curl https://api.sandbox.northlinepay.example/v1/refunds \
  -u sk_test_YOUR_SECRET_KEY: \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 2b1a9c44-0e5d-4f1a-9c33-aa10e2d8b771" \
  -d '{
    "payment": "pay_3k91ab20",
    "amount": 500,
    "reason": "requested_by_customer"
  }'

Error codes

Retry only errors marked retryable, and only with the same idempotency key. Card declines are final for that attempt — ask the customer for another method rather than looping.

HTTPCodeMeaningRetry
400invalid_requestMissing or malformed field. error.param names the field.No
401authentication_failedMissing, revoked, or wrong-environment API key.No
402card_declinedIssuer declined. See decline_code (insufficient_funds, lost_card, do_not_honor).No
402expired_cardCard expiry is in the past.No
403permission_deniedKey lacks the scope, or the resource belongs to another account.No
404resource_missingUnknown payment, customer, or refund ID.No
409idempotency_key_reusedSame key sent with a different request body.No
409payment_already_capturedCapture called on a payment that is already captured or refunded.No
422amount_too_smallAmount is below the currency minimum.No
429rate_limit_exceededToo many requests. Honor Retry-After.Yes
500api_errorUnexpected server error. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key.Yes
503service_unavailableTemporary outage or maintenance.Yes

Every error response includes request_id. Include it when contacting support.

Webhooks

Register an HTTPS endpoint that returns 2xx within 10 seconds. The API delivers events as POST requests with Content-Type: application/json. Delivery is at-least-once: your handler must be idempotent on event.id.

Signature

Each delivery includes Northline-Signature:

t=1730470928,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd

Compute HMAC-SHA256 over {t}.{raw_body} using the endpoint’s signing secret (whsec_…), and compare to v1 with a constant-time compare. Reject timestamps older than five minutes to limit replay. Do not parse the body before verifying.

Event envelope

{
  "id": "evt_44b91e",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "payment.succeeded",
  "created": "2026-11-01T14:22:09Z",
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "pay_3k91ab20",
      "object": "payment",
      "amount": 2499,
      "currency": "usd",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "metadata": { "order_id": "10482" }
    }
  }
}
EventWhen it fires
payment.succeededA payment is captured and funds are pending settlement.
payment.failedAuthorization or capture failed after an async step.
payment.requires_actionThe customer must complete 3-D Secure or a bank redirect.
refund.succeededA refund has been accepted by the network.
refund.failedA refund could not be processed. The payment remains captured.

Failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for 72 hours. Return 2xx only after you have durably recorded the event. Use the dashboard to resend a single event while integrating.

Rate limits

Limits are applied per API key and reset on a rolling window. When you exceed a limit the API returns 429 with code: rate_limit_exceeded and a Retry-After header in seconds. Back off at least that long, then retry with the original idempotency key.

ScopeLimit
Read requests (GET)100 requests / second
Write requests (POST)25 requests / second
Payment creates, per key50 requests / second burst, sustained 20 / second
Test-mode keysSame ceilings, plus a daily cap of 1,000 payment creates

Response headers on every call:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit — ceiling for this route class.
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining — requests left in the current window.
  • X-RateLimit-Reset — unix timestamp when the window resets.
Do not poll GET /payments/{id} for status. Subscribe to webhooks and fetch the payment only when you need the full object.

Need a higher ceiling for a launch or a batch import? Contact support with your expected peak requests per second and the key prefix. Increases are granted per live key, not account-wide.
